Hi Marc — thanks, and great to hear the demo landed. Looping in Karthik (deploy/runbook) and Neha (security/compliance) to confirm the operational details and supply a draft MOP.

Quick summary from me while they pull specifics:
- Region-pin = tenant compute + persistent volumes + object snapshots pinned to the chosen cloud region/availability zones; cross-region replication is not enabled by default.
- Backups: automated snapshots are retained according to the retention policy you choose; they are stored in the same region unless you explicitly enable cross-region replication (this is an opt-in feature and requires an enterprise policy).
- Wipe/termination: we run a tenant teardown that deletes live volumes, then issues snapshot deletion jobs and a backup sweep. We'll provide timing estimates and the MOP draft.

Attaching a simple network/flow diagram and a first-pass MOP (draft). Karthik / Neha — can you confirm SLA for backup purge timing, and any edge cases (e.g., archived cold storage or third-party transfer)?

Hi all — technical confirmation below and a few important caveats. I'm pasting the trimmed answers you can put straight into your control file.

Operational definition (short):
- Region-pinning ensures tenant compute (VMs/containers), primary block storage, and any object storage snapshots are created and retained in the selected cloud region and its AZs. We do not route live inference traffic through other regions for that tenant by default.

Backup replication behavior:
- Default: snapshots and incremental backups are stored in the same region. No automatic cross-region replication.
- Opt-in cross-region replication: available as an add-on when customers require multi-region DR; enabling requires config change + approval and will be reflected in billing.
- Archive/long-term: If you choose long-term archival to a lower-cost tier, that data remains in-region unless an explicit cross-region archival target is configured.

Deletion / Rollback MOP (summary):
1) Submit termination request via Console/API with tenant id.
2) Quiesce active jobs and drain KV caches (few seconds — minutes depending on load).
3) Delete live volumes and immediately mark snapshots for deletion.
4) Enqueue snapshot deletion jobs that run at controlled throughput to avoid API throttling; job status is available in the Console.
5) Run backup-sweep job to remove any object-store artifacts (includes cleaning of multipart uploads and temporary manifests).
6) Final verification by ops: checksum/manifest audit and issuance of a wipe certificate.

Timing expectations (typical):
- Live volumes deleted: within minutes of scheduling (subject to size).
- Snapshot deletion sweep: completes within 24–72 hours for standard retention sizes; large accounts (>100 TB) may take up to 10 days to fully purge depending on chunking and provider API limits.
- Archival tiers: if your data was moved to long-term archive, purge may take up to 30 days depending on provider restore/expunge windows.

Edge cases:
- If you've enabled cross-region replication we will need to run delete jobs in both regions and coordinate with partner cloud accounts — that adds time.
- If a customer requested encrypted snapshots with a customer-managed key (CMK) and you later revoke key access, we treat snapshots as inaccessible; for verifiable deletion we recommend key rotation + deletion policy in parallel.

I've added a short MOP PDF (draft) with exact CLI steps and a runbook link you can use for audit evidence.

-Karthik
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference

Marc — adding the compliance perspective. Important to call out a couple points auditors always ask for:

1) Evidence artifacts we can provide: tenant deployment manifest (region + AZs), snapshot deletion logs with timestamps, ops-issued wipe certificate, and runbook/CLI trace shown in the MOP. We can provide signed PDFs for audit.
2) Immutable logs: audit logs for deletion jobs are retained in our control plane; we can provide time-bounded exports but customers should also maintain an archival copy.
3) Cryptography: all data at rest is encrypted. If you use customer-managed keys (CMK), make sure your key policy allows Redwoods' deletion flows (we cannot delete snapshots if we lose access to the CMK — see Karthik's note).

Recommended language for your control file (one line each):
- "Redwood Dedicated: tenant compute, block volumes, and snapshots are pinned to the selected cloud region and AZs; no cross-region replication occurs unless explicitly enabled."
- "Upon tenant termination Redwood executes a documented wipe MOP: live volume deletion, snapshot enqueue-and-expunge, backup-sweep, and final manifest audit. Typical completion ranges from 24 hours to 10 days depending on data volume and provider limits; archival tier purges may take up to 30 days."

If you need, we can produce a signed one-page MOP summary on company letterhead for your control file.

-Neha Kapoor
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
